title: ArcelorMittal Halts Ukraine's Largest Steel Plant After Repeated Russian Strikes, Books $1B Charge
detail: ArcelorMittal announced on September 26 that it can no longer safely and sustainably operate its Kryvyi Rih plant — Ukraine's largest steelmaker, producing 1.7 million tonnes of steel and 1.6 million tonnes of rolled products in 2025 (23% and 24% of national output) — after four Russian missile strikes over five weeks killed 5 workers and injured 17, including an August 16 strike (2 killed, 13 injured, blast furnace and energy units damaged) and a further attack on September 21. The company expects to book a roughly $1 billion non-cash impairment charge and said it has provided about $700 million in financial support to the plant since the February 2022 invasion. CEO Mauro Longobardo said the company is discussing the plant's future with the Ukrainian government while focusing on preserving infrastructure for an eventual restart. The shutdown means all three of Ukraine's main steel plants, which together accounted for roughly 90% of national steel production, are now offline due to repeated Russian strikes.

title: Trump Presses Zelensky to Accept Deal with Putin Amid Ongoing Russian Strikes
detail: US President Donald Trump publicly urged Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to make a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to end the Ukraine conflict, signaling a sharp increase in US diplomatic pressure on Kyiv. The pressure comes as Zelensky had recently made an appeal at the United Nations and as Russian strikes continue across Ukraine. The statement reinforces the Trump administration's stance that a negotiated settlement is the preferred path to ending the war, placing additional strain on the US-Ukraine relationship at a critical juncture in the conflict.

title: Russian Glide Bombs Kill Up to 3 at Sumy Family Support Centre, 28 Injured Including Children
detail: Russian forces struck Sumy with three glide bombs on the evening of September 26, hitting near a family/cultural support centre and damaging two kindergartens, dozens of residential buildings, administrative buildings and over 20 vehicles. Sumy Oblast Governor Oleh Hryhorov initially reported 2 killed and 23 injured, including 4 children — three girls aged 14 and 8 and an 11-month-old infant, plus two adults, were hospitalized. By September 27, Interior Minister Ivan Vyhivskyi said the confirmed toll had risen to 3 killed, including a 16-year-old girl, with the regional injury count reaching 28 as further victims were treated. The strike came days after Trump and Zelensky met at the UN to discuss a ceasefire, despite which Russia continued large-scale attacks.

title: Ukraine Strikes Azov Optical-Mechanical Plant in Rostov Oblast with Neptune Missiles and Drone-Missiles
detail: Ukrainian forces struck the Azov Optical-Mechanical Plant in Rostov Oblast, part of Russia's Tactical Missiles Corporation, using Neptune cruise missiles and Ruta, Palianytsia and Bars drone-missiles in a joint operation by the Special Operations Center and Navy. The General Staff reported fires and damage to optical and foundry production, the assembly section, the electroplating shop and the printed circuit board shop. The plant supplies components for Russian missile programmes. Damage assessment is preliminary.
